lesson_verdict.length_tone: PASS: 6 narrative sections 160-293 words, narrative 1,471 words, no paragraph over 90 words (block quotes exempt), no trap language.
defects: Section 'Reform bent, it did not break': 'The compulsory draft began in the last quarter of the 16th century, taking about one in seven men for farm work and about four percent for the mines.' Both figures are misassigned. The one-seventh figure is the Andean mita for the Potosi/Huancavelica MINES (Toledo, 1570s), not farm work; the 4% figure is the New Spain repartimiento weekly levy (1588 Taxco rule, all enterprises), while Britannica gives about 5% for mines and about 10% more for seasonal agricultural work. The sentence reverses the association. Fix in the lesson, e.g. attribute the one-in-seven figure to the mita for the Potosi mines and the 4-5% figure to the New Spain repartimiento levy.

Section 'Why the labor force changed': 'The first asiento was granted in August 1518 to Laurent de Gouvenot, for eight years and a maximum of 4,000 people, at a price of 25,000 ducats.' The details (August 1518, Gouvenot, eight years, 4,000) are correct, but 'at a price of 25,000 ducats' misattributes the payment: Gouvenot received the grant and SOLD the license to Genoese merchants for 25,000 ducats; he did not pay that price to the Crown. Fix in the lesson: 'Gouvenot promptly sold the license to Genoese merchants for 25,000 ducats.'
notes: Voodoo suspicion withdrawn: Princeton Ch. 6 supplement says verbatim 'Religions such as voodoo are a blend of Christianity and tribal animism. Enslaved people sang African songs in the fields as they worked' — the lesson follows its grounding book.
Palmares in Brazil is Barron's own content (Ch. 3: early 1600s, more than 30,000, conquered by the Portuguese in 1694); the lesson correctly names Brazil and Portuguese forces.
The two-republics system is not in the three book chapters but is standard and correct (republica de espanoles / republica de indios, separate towns, officials, and obligations).

The New Laws' content is not mentioned in the three chapters; the lesson cites the New Laws (1542) as a primary source and the content (free subjects, no new grants, grants end at the holder's death, no enslavement) is standard.

Interpretive gloss with no direct book support: 'The men who profited from the encomienda sat on the councils that were supposed to enforce the New Laws.' Plausible, but the lesson's own analysis, not a book fact.

Valladolid debate 1550-1551 and 'Sepulveda never visited the Americas' are not in the three book chapters but are confirmed by standard sources; the lesson's phrasing 'Las Casas argued against Sepulveda' is the standard shorthand for sequential presentations to the royal committee, which reached no verdict.

apush-leq-0008.reason: Model outline thesis and rubric analysis criterion require a point the lesson never teaches: 'wealth could soften a rank without erasing it' / 'mixing and wealth could shift a person's lived position.' The lesson teaches mixing producing new categories, but nothing about wealth softening rank, and the formal mechanism for it (gracias al sacar) is late 18th century, outside the 1500-1607 window. A student working only from the lesson cannot earn the analysis points as written. Fix in the question: drop 'and wealth' from the rubric analysis criterion and the wealth clause from the model thesis; the mixing point the lesson teaches carries the complexity.
